## Scope and terms

**資料範圍**：此例是教學模型，不是已查證的服務實作。
Client sends a complete document to API, the Document API that validates requests.
Store is the Document Store that owns persistence inside the service.
A revision is the stored version number used to reject stale replacements.

slides.title: Service boundary
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Client["Client"] --> Api["API"]
  subgraph Backend["Service 服務"]
    Api --> Store["Store"]
  end
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Client stays outside the service boundary.
API accepts the request, while Store owns the persistent document.

slides.title: Validation and handoff
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Client["Client"] --> Api["API"]
  subgraph ApiDetail["API internals"]
    Api --> Validator["Validator"]
    Validator --> Handler["Handler"]
  end
  Handler --> Store["Store"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Inside API, Validator checks the complete document before any storage operation.
Handler passes an accepted request to Store; invalid input stops without a write.

slides.title: Serialized commit
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Api["API"] --> Store["Store"]
  subgraph StorageDetail["Store internals"]
    Store --> Queue["Queue"]
    Queue --> Revision["Revision check"]
    Revision --> Temp["Temp JSON"]
    Temp --> Commit["Rename"]
    Commit --> Files["Files"]
  end

blocks.markdown:
## Latency model

For an accepted request, $T = T_{api} + T_{store}$.
$T_{api}$ covers validation and handling, while $T_{store}$ covers queueing and writing:

$$
T_{store} = T_{queue} + T_{write}
$$

These terms describe a simple model, not measured performance.
The public interface below separates the caller's contract from the service's private write path.

slides.title: Caller contract
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Client submits the complete document and expected revision to API.
The response reports the saved revision without exposing Store's internal write steps.

blocks.markdown:
## Conclusion

Validation protects the input boundary; serialized revision checks and atomic replacement protect the write boundary.
A conflict requires a fresh read, while a successful save confirms persistence, not rendering.
Verify this teaching model against the implementation before using it as an operational guide.
